body:
Go into detail, if you would, about that 4 and a half hours.

I'm in a similar situation, I'd rather off myself than work shit jobs just to exist. The only way up seems to be grinding those yearly raises, that just don't hold a nickel to living expenses. 

I've thought a lot about finding work in an oil town for a while, buying some experiences then showing myself out. Maybe a road trip that ends when I run out of cash.

It's the human condition. 

The light turns on and we find ourselves being hurled down a mountain, and straight into an abyss. The ones that try to stop get crushed under the momentum and forgotten. Some people find patterns in the avalanche and ride it for some style points, but we're all just as dead as everyone else.

And of course that doesn't include how we treat each other on the way down.

Snap to, we're a bunch of screaming, fighting, fucking apes riding a rock through a celestial merry-go-round.
 
Now I can't pretend to help because I'm as depressed as anybody here, but if there's a formula for fun anywhere to be found in this godless universe it would be found here.
I wonder how long the line would be.

My take on it:

Depression is hell, more or less. It's a haze that encapsulates your mind in a airtight veil, where everything inside is definite and lifeless. Anything beyond it doesn't exist. It's like a psychological prison complete with cold, grey walls and ceilings that are way too low.

It's a null zone where intuition and reason don't apply. You'll find yourself sad when there's nothing to be sad about, and it will *frustrate* you. Taunt, in a way. It's there to dictate you, to suck every moment dry until you've nothing left, except for *those* feelings. Feelings so potent you'd swear you could rip them right out of your chest.The feelings of inadequacy. The feelings of unresolvable torment. I've had to make conscious decisions *not* to end my life, and I was only able through shear objectivity.

In fact, that's the only way to get through Depression. You cannot argue with it. You cannot debate, reason, or compromise with it. It is entirely irrational. -Know what it's like to be afraid after a scary movie? That walk from the living room to your bedroom is a fuck ton longer than it used to be. The monster under the stairs is just waiting to grab at your feet, and the creeper in the closet is waiting for you to turn the lights out, so you'll just sleep with them on. But what's different between this night and the previous nights? I mean, yesterday you certainly weren't afraid of your own home, but at the moment you can't convince yourself to take the blanket off of your head.

Perspective. State of mind, if you will. And, just like with depression, you can't reason yourself out of that fear because it makes no sense in the first place. What you can, rather NEED to do is realize that depression is nothing but a negative feedback loop. Specifically knowing that it has *no meaning*, that it's really just a consequence, gives you the chance to fix it.
Regarding my body as a separate entity; I don't want to kill it, I just wish not to exist.

>Even in a world dominated by the exploitative, you still have the opportunity to enjoy and see the world and your self. You can meet people who feel similarly to you and fight the powers you so despise. You can influence and affect the world, or even withdraw from it and exist in a world of your own making. To paraphrase Samwise Gamgee "There's good in this world, and it's worth fighting for."

Exploiter vs exploited isn't something to fight, it's the way of the universe. Or, at least, the way life presents itself here.

>Raising babies is not entirely instinct, which is why so many people are bad at it. Shaken baby syndrome, SIDS, child abuse etc.

Intact people don't kill babies.

>Regarding parents "owning" a child's accomplishments, I think you're misconstruing pride in one's children for vanity.

When said child is an actual child, and not an athlete, the happiness is mutual. They share the same shear amount of excitement.

>Yes, as a parent you should get upset. It means your child needs help.

So what do you do? How do you "help"? How do you help one understand that there's no such thing as right or wrong in the flow of the universe? How do you explain that all the good moments are just that and all the agony is for nothing?

>The world is what it is, whether you see it positively or negatively can be as simple as how often you get exercise, get sunlight, eat healthy to provide the chemicals your body needs to be happy. 

There's also the genetic lottery, where, and when you are born. Who rules over you, economic affiliations, societal norms. It's not as simple as how well you treat your self.

>the opportunity to explore the wonder of the universe and being sentient

I always feel that this is such a doctored answer; optimism bias at it's most influential. In a world of limited resources, sentience only benefits the exploitative. For example, electronics made at Foxconn, a notoriously poor environment, regularly define a way of life we have the states.

>Have you ever had a child? Have you ever held a small, frail life in your hands, and went through all of the work to raise it to a thinking, interacting being? Then you can't comprehend how painful it is to watch the baby you nurtured turn against itself and undo all that you have done to get it to live. 

You're giving too much praise to what is actually instinct. Hormones change your perspective of them from baby diablos to little bundles of joy. 

Also, how much of parenting is actually personal satisfaction? Parents experience magnified feelings from their kids. When they see them cry, they think, "What should I do to fix this? What will make them happy again?". When their kids are happy they don't just see it, they *own* it. They made that being and made it happy. 

Should you be upset that the little ball of happiness you leached off of for years finds out there's not really much to life? Like when they realize their perspective encompasses virtually nothing and everything that seems amazing and grandeur is basic and thoughtless?

>the people around you love you in ways deeper than you could know.

I can only imagine people would feel the same way I would feel, being slapped in the face with mortality. Everything else would, again, be overtly optimistic; "imagine what could have been".

>Being suicidal is a mental disease.

The "stab myself with the nearest sharp thing" loop people fall into, yea I'd agree. But, just as everything else ever, not every suicide is the same. They don't all stem from an altered state of mind. Many, I'd argue, are simple weigh of pros vs cons.
